name: Esther
bio:
Esther, also called Hadassah, was a Jewish orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai in Susa after her parents' death. When King Ahasuerus searched his empire for a new queen after deposing Vashti, Esther was gathered among the young women brought to the palace and placed under the care of Hegai, keeper of the harem, who favored her above the rest; following Mordecai's instruction, she kept her Jewish identity hidden. After a year of beauty preparations, Esther pleased the king more than any other woman, and he crowned her queen in his seventh year, celebrating with a great feast and a tax relief for the provinces. She continued to follow Mordecai's guidance, and through him reported a plot by two chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, to assassinate the king, which was investigated and the plotters executed (Esther 2:7-23). Her decisive role in saving her people from Haman's plot is told in detail in the chapters ahead.

 When Esther learned through Hatach of Haman's decree, she feared approaching the king unsummoned could mean death, but Mordecai's warning that she would not escape either, and his question of whether she had come to her position for exactly this moment, moved her to resolve: she would go to the king even though it broke the law, and if she perished, she perished. She asked Mordecai to have the Jews of Susa join her in a three-day fast beforehand (Esther 4:4-17).

 On the third day of the fast, Esther put on her royal robes and stood in the inner court; the king, pleased to see her, extended his scepter and offered her up to half the kingdom. Rather than state her request immediately, Esther invited Ahasuerus and Haman to a banquet that day, and at the banquet invited them to a second one the next day, where she would finally make her request (Esther 5:1-8).
